parole.testo: Probably borrowed from English agnostic, ultimately from Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-, “not”) + γιγνώσκω (gignṓskō, “I know”); influenced by existing agentive suffix -ик (-yk).

parole.significato: Baptist (member of a Baptist church or denomination)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English Baptist, from Ancient Greek βαπτιστής (baptistḗs). By surface analysis, Ancient Greek βάπτω (báptō) + -и́ст (-ýst).
Borrowed from English genetics, from Ancient Greek γένεσις (génesis).
Borrowed from English empathy, from Ancient Greek ἐμπάθεια (empátheia). Compare Russian эмпа́тия (empátija), Belarusian эмпа́тыя (empátyja), Polish empatia.

Borrowed from English palaeolith, paleolith, from palaeolithic, paleolithic, from Ancient Greek παλαιός (palaiós, “old”) and λίθος (líthos, “stone”). Compare Russian палеоли́т (paleolít), Belarusian палеалі́т (paljealít), Polish paleolit.
Borrowed from English photon, ultimately from Ancient Greek φῶς, φωτός (phôs, phōtós).

parole.significato: cyclone (weather phenomenon consisting of a system of winds rotating around a centre of low atmospheric pressure)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English cyclone, from Ancient Greek κύκλος (kúklos).
Borrowed from English isotope, from Ancient Greek ἴσος (ísos, “equal”) and τόπος (tópos, “place”). Compare Russian изото́п (izotóp), Belarusian ізато́п (izatóp), Polish izotop.
